raw_response:
I am getting older now, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. Six mu is not much land, but every mu must earn something. I mostly do what has worked for me before. In our county, vegetables can make money, but they also need more watching than wheat or maize. I have well water, so I am not as afraid of dry weather, but pumping costs money, so I cannot water too often for no reason.

For this year, I will keep the land mainly in the way I know: on 3 mu I will do `cabbage -> Chinese cabbage -> cabbage` in sequence, because that is the rotation I am used to and I can manage it with two people in the house. On the other 3 mu, I will keep some chili and kidney bean so I am not betting everything on one vegetable. If cabbage price falls, maybe chili or beans can help. I do not read many technical papers, so I look at my own field, what the neighbors do, and what I can afford. I use enough fertilizer to keep the crop looking strong, but not so much that I have no cash left. Water I will use when the soil turns dry and after transplanting, because seedlings are the most delicate time.
